correctness.rationale: D has forced block form (A,0;B,T_A), and squaring gives A²=T_A²=0 and T_AB+BA=0. The exterior-square identity T_A²=2 wedge²A yields allowed ranks. In a squarezero Jordan basis rank T_A=r(n-r-1), so Hom over the dual-number algebra has dimension h_r. Counting square-zero A by its image/kernel/isomorphism gives the Gaussian product, with no missing boundary cases. Exhaustive independent small-prime-field computations reproduce counts for n=3 q=2,3 and n=4 q=2. Leading q-degrees prove the asymptotic phase transition.

value.rationale: The square-zero locus is a canonical nilpotent algebraic subset of the derivation algebra of a universal Lie object. A complete exact rank-stratified q-enumerator and a characteristic-two admissibility jump are structural data for every rank n>=3, not a single computational slice or an idempotent substitution. The asymptotic central-derivation transition at n=3/4 is a motivated additional invariant; the fixed formula is not implied by the known all-derivation parametrization.
